Diane / team —

A few technical notes to help you evaluate region/scale choices and autoscale behaviour (high level):

1) Pool sizing and burst model
- Initial committed pool: 8 A100-equivalent slots (we expose as "units"). Minimum pool will be 6 units to preserve baseline latency; max pool for autoscale set to 12 units by default.
- Burst headroom: We use a transient burst queue for short spikes (up to configured credit). Sustained spikes above 30 minutes will push autoscaler to spin additional capacity (subject to available regional inventory).
- Latency: under steady-state within committed capacity you should expect median token-level latency similar to our hosted profiles (single-digit ms for model compute). During transient bursts where the system uses pre-warmed burst capacity, tail latency may increase up to 2–3x for affected requests. For sustained scaling (autoscale adding instances) there is ~90–180s spin-up time depending on instance type.

2) Regional constraints and recommendations
- Primary: us-west-2 — best inventory and lowest latency for your users.
- DR/secondary: eu-west-1 recommended if you want multi-region failover; note pricing and instance availability vary — we’ll show you a capacity view in the kickoff call.

3) Networking / security pre-reqs
- We support customer-managed KMS; we will need a service principal set up and an IAM role for Redwood to write audit logs.
- VPC peering works; we also support transit gateway if you prefer. NAT/proxies should allow outbound to our control-plane endpoints (we’ll list exact IP ranges in the runbook).

4) Activation milestones and time estimates
- Provisioning (pool creation & test): 2 business days after SOW + network ready
- Integration testing (prefix caching, KV warmups): 3–5 business days
- Production cutover / smoke: 1 day

I’ll bring a capacity plan and an ops checklist to the kickoff.

—karthik
